input.charter:
# Charter — S10 Copilot / AG-UI (retrospective, 2026-11-27)

- **Project:** S10 'Copilot / AG-UI — one action surface, proposals, conversations', track v1, ADM phase G, delivery plateau, tranche 6, plan `docs/plans/slices/S10-copilot-ag-ui.md`.
- **Sponsor:** the programme's sponsoring group, through the tranche-6 PI plan and the standing delegation `01a1fb9f-ac2d-732d-b274-1079be3dd2b3`.
- **Authority:** SPEC §8 S10 sets the gate: a scripted agent session passes. SPEC D14 keeps inference-router outside the conveyor, and D17 makes the web, MCP and messaging channels equivalent over one action and one approval row. The slice's own decisions S10-D1 to S10-D7 are recorded in the plan.
- **Objective:** an agent operates the app through the S04 registry. The tool list is a projection of `ActionSpec`s filtered by the caller's scopes; a destructive tool call becomes an S06 approval; the conversation is two tables plus an SSE stream; and the copilot does not grow a second action system.
- **Scope in:** `conversation` and `conversation_turn`; the turn runner; the agent-surface projection and its coverage test; proposals as `approval(kind='copilot.action')`; the execution claim and sweep; SSE `conversation:{id}` with `Last-Event-ID` replay; `completions.create` as a fail-closed external action; the AG-UI serializer; and the screens declared as data for S12.
- **Scope out:** `inference-router` (D14), the `/mcp` transport and scope filtering (S04), the approval state machine (S06), fr's 34 `agui/actions` modules and `agent-core`, the agent's tool contract and principal (S06b), and chat UI rendering (S12).
- **Constraints:** one registry, so `/api/copilot/actions` and `/mcp` `tools/list` are renderings of the same answer; a tool effect is an `action_invocation`; a proposal carries the exact input sealed under the tenant key and a redacted projection in the approval row; approvals never expire; execution uses a conditional claim and `Idempotency-Key: proposal:<approval_id>`; an unavailable model ends the turn `failed` with zero tool invocations; the only coverage exemption is the `copilot.chat` transport route.
- **Retrospective status:** the capability is built in the tree. It is evidenced by fourteen `crates/api/tests/copilot_*.rs` suites, `crates/api/tests/agui_parity.rs`, `crates/actions/tests/copilot_coverage.rs`, `migrations/0018_copilot.sql` and the modules named below. The project row was created on 2026-11-12, later closed, and measured `built`; the pre-pack receipt `docs/evidence/rework/S10.json` (2026-11-25) was red on the lifecycle and tranche checks. This charter and the set that follows are authored retrospectively at the 2026-11-27 snapshot and do not attest contemporaneous ceremonial review. No deployed copilot, chat UI or production router run is claimed; those stay S12 and S14 work.

body.acceptance_criteria: The gate is a scripted session: open a conversation, ask for a card move, receive a proposal and one pending approval with zero action invocations; approve as an authorized member and see exactly one invocation, the card moved and the turn completed citing that invocation; reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` and receive the turn once; see a low-scope principal's two surfaces omit the same tool; see an unavailable router fail the turn with zero invocations; and see the coverage gate fail an unmapped operation by name. The local proofs are `crates/api/tests/copilot_session.rs`, `copilot_proposal.rs`, `copilot_approve.rs`, `copilot_replay.rs`, `copilot_surface.rs`, `copilot_turn.rs` and `crates/actions/tests/copilot_coverage.rs`.
body.assignment: The architecture work assigns S10 the copilot's one action surface: project the S04 registry by principal, turn a destructive tool call into an S06 approval, run the conversation as two tables and an event stream, and keep model access outside the conveyor. This statement governs the retrospective record of work built in the S10 slice and re-read at the 2026-11-27 snapshot.
body.constraints: S10-D1 keeps the surface a query over `ActionSpec`, so no second registry or tool table exists. S10-D2 makes a proposal an approval created through S06's `insert_approval_tx`, with one pending proposal per turn enforced by the partial unique index on `(tenant_id, meta->>'turn_id')`. S10-D3 makes execution a job with a conditional claim, a 120-second lease, re-checked proposer scopes and the proposal idempotency key. S10-D4 makes only terminal turns durable, with the terminal meta, the proposal and the `conversation_turn.created` event committed together. S10-D5 makes `completions.create` fail closed: an outage, timeout or open breaker ends the turn `failed` and runs no tool. S10-D6 declares `copilot.chat` the only coverage exemption. S10-D7 keeps AG-UI as a serializer over the native stream.
body.responsibilities: The programme architect authors this retrospective statement; the delivery team (conveyor-e2e) is accountable for the evidence; the Architecture Board reviews the artefact set; the SRO accepts the project's closure at the tranche-6 review. S12 is consulted as the renderer of the declared screens, operations is consulted on model availability and key custody, and the tenant admin is consulted because the channel grants and the approval decision are the authorization surface.
body.retrospective: This statement of architecture work is authored on 2026-11-27 for the tranche-6 rework. No contemporaneous SoAW exists; the S10 row was created on 2026-11-12 and the build was recorded in the slice plan and the receipt. The statement records what the tree and the suites prove today, names the pre-pack receipt as red on lifecycle checks, and leaves the deployed UI and router proof to S12 and S14 instead of implying it happened.
body.scope: In scope are the `conversation` and `conversation_turn` tables with forced row-level security, the turn runner and its eight-round cap, the `agent_surface` projection over the action registry, proposals carried as `approval(kind='copilot.action')` with sealed inputs, the conditional execution claim and sweep, the SSE topic `conversation:{id}` with `Last-Event-ID` replay, `completions.create` as an external action with a 60-second timeout and breaker, the AG-UI serializer, and the screens declared as data for S12. Out of scope are inference-router (D14), the `/mcp` transport and scope filtering (S04), the approval state machine (S06), fr's 34 AG-UI action modules, the agent's principal and tool contract (S06b), and chat UI rendering (S12).

input.body: The copilot does not absorb inference-router (D14). `completions.create` is an external action with a 60-second timeout and a process-local breaker; an outage, a timeout or an open breaker ends the turn `failed` with zero tool invocations. The fail-closed rule is deliberate, but it makes the conversation unavailable whenever the router is, and the suite proves the refusal rather than a fallback.
input.response: Track the router's availability with the estate's external probe and record any outage during a delivery window; if the failure rate is material, revisit the retry budget with S14 rather than adding a heuristic substitute.
input.title: The model boundary is external, so a router outage stops every turn

input.body: Execution takes a conditional claim with a 120-second lease, re-checks the proposer's scopes and invokes under the proposal idempotency key. The crash-replay and double-decision suites prove the tested cases, but a live estate with concurrent workers and long-running actions can still exercise lease expiry and worker replacement in ways a single-process suite does not measure. The risk is a duplicated effect, not a lost approval.
input.response: At S14, run the proposal execution with two workers against the deployed queue, record the invocation count for a forced kill between claim and invoke, and re-read this risk against that receipt.
input.title: Exactly-once execution depends on the claim lease and the idempotency key together

input.body: A secret-bearing action's exact input is sealed with the tenant key in the approval row and only the redacted projection is readable by members. Execution refuses when the seal cannot be opened, which is the safe outcome, but a key rotation or a missing KEK during a delivery window can strand an approved proposal until operations restores the key. The risk is availability of a pending decision, not exposure of the secret.
input.response: Include proposal execution in the key-rotation runbook, alert on the refusal path, and record the tenant key id on the approval row so a restored key can be matched to the pending proposal.
input.title: A sealed proposal input depends on the tenant key being available at execution

input.body: The plan keeps AG-UI only if S0 parity evidence shows a live consumer, and the tree keeps `agui.rs` as a serializer over the native stream. `agui_parity.rs` proves that a completed turn serializes to the golden frames and that every frame type is one of fr's eight; it does not prove that a deployed consumer reads them. The adapter could be dead weight, and the open question in the plan remains open.
input.response: At S14, measure `/api/agui*` ingress before and after cutover; if no live consumer appears, record the dropped rows in `parity.yaml` and remove the adapter rather than carrying it on faith.
input.title: The AG-UI adapter's live consumer is not proven by the golden-frame suite

input.body: A call whose effect is destructive, whose confirmation is not none or whose hints require a proposal is not executed; it creates one `approval(kind='copilot.action')` in the same transaction as the terminal turn, with the exact input sealed and the approval target recorded. The benefit is an auditable question before the effect, proven by the proposal, approval and destructive-target suites.
input.title: A destructive tool call becomes a decidable approval

input.body: The two conversation tables record the dialogue, while tool calls remain `action_invocation` rows cited from the turn meta. The terminal turn and its event commit together, so a reconnect replays the turn once and a crash leaves an interrupted turn rather than a claimed effect. The benefit is a record that can be audited without reconstructing a parallel log.
input.title: Conversations are durable and replayable without a second execution log

input.body: `copilot_coverage.rs` asserts that every mutating action is in the surface, that an injected unmapped operation is returned by name, and that the one transport exemption is declared. The benefit is preventive: a new screen element that forgets its action fails the build instead of silently joining an allowlist, which is the failure the plan's trap 1 names.
input.title: The coverage gate fails by name rather than widening an exemption

input.body: The approval row is readable by every member who may list approvals, so the exact input is sealed under the tenant key and the visible input and diff redact every `x-secret` property at any depth. Execution replays only the sealed value and refuses when the seal cannot be opened. The benefit is that a person can decide a secret-bearing action without the secret becoming conversation content.
input.title: A proposal does not expose a secret-bearing input to approvers

# Closure Review — S10 Copilot / AG-UI (retrospective, 2026-11-27)

## Outcome vs acceptance

The outcome is a copilot that operates the app through one action surface, turns a destructive call into a decidable approval, records a durable conversation and replays it without a second effect. Against the plan's section 7 properties, the local proof covers the scripted session, approval-gated execution, the second decision, reconnect replay, the scope-absent tool, the inference outage and the coverage gate. The chat UI rendering and the deployed copilot and router runs are S12 and S14 work and are recorded as deferred rather than met. The retrospective level is compliant for the record set because the pack supplies the lifecycle and the suites carry the local proof.

## Evidence

The evidence is the fourteen `crates/api/tests/copilot_*.rs` suites, `crates/api/tests/agui_parity.rs`, `crates/actions/tests/copilot_coverage.rs`, the migration `migrations/0018_copilot.sql`, the pre-pack receipt `docs/evidence/rework/S10.json` generated on 2026-11-25, and the seventeen checks in `acceptance/programme/S10.toml`. The Phase-G review records the same set, names the pre-pack receipt as red on lifecycle checks, and names the deferred items explicitly.

## Open items

The chat UI, the deployed copilot run and the production router proof are S12 and S14 work. The AG-UI adapter's live consumer remains an open question and is registered as S10-R4. The plan's stale deliverable paths and the agent-surface module header contradiction are carried as S10-I2 and S10-I3. The extra suites, including the S16 W7 identity tests, are recorded in S10-I4 and are not re-scoped to this project.

## Decision

The project is closed. The closure is taken by an approver other than the requester under the standing delegation, the closure review is recorded in the same pack, and the tranche-6 review is the forum that accepts it. No waiver is claimed, and no check in the manifest is weakened to reach this decision.

# Project Brief — S10 Copilot / AG-UI (retrospective, 2026-11-27)

## Outcome

A person or an agent operates the app through one action surface: the tool list is the projection of the registry the caller's scopes admit, a destructive tool call becomes an approval a person can decide, and the conversation is recorded as two tables plus an event stream. The outcome is true in the tree at the route and test-database boundary and is exercised by the copilot suites; a deployed chat UI and a production router run are not claimed.

## Boundary

S10 owns the conversation tables, the turn runner, the agent-surface projection, proposals as copilot approvals, the execution claim and sweep, SSE replay, the external completion action and the AG-UI serializer. It does not own the `/mcp` transport or scope filtering (S04), the approval state machine (S06), the agent's principal and tool contract (S06b), inference-router (D14), or the chat UI rendering (S12, contract section 11).

## Reuse sources

The plan's source table names what S10 reads from S04, S06 and the fr AG-UI surface. The build reuses the `ActionSpec` registry and `invoke`, the `approval` and `approval_decision` rows, `insert_approval_tx`, the outbox event and SSE replay, and the S16 prompt-audit identity for the copilot system message. Nothing from fr's 34 action modules or `HeuristicIntentResolver` is carried.

## Inception units

The plan's build order is the inception sequence: preflight, the parity check, the copilot migration, the domain and store functions, the agent surface, the actions route, the external completion, the turn runner, the proposal path, execution and sweep, SSE and the reaper, the coverage test, the AG-UI adapter, and the gate. The tree shows the sequence landed; the extra suites record the defects found after it, including the destructive-target regression and the crash replay case.

## Dependencies

S02 supplies the event and audit substrate; S03 the approval storage and tenant row-level security; S04 the registry, the `/mcp` transport and the invocation path; S06 the approval state machine and decision route. S12 renders the declared screens and S14 carries the deployed cutover proof. S06b's agent principal is the machine consumer of the same projection, recorded as a seam because the project row's depends_on list does not include it.

## Acceptance

The plan's section 7 property table is the acceptance: the scripted session, approval-gated execution, a second decision, reconnect replay, the scope-absent tool, the inference outage and the coverage gate. The local proofs are the fourteen copilot suites and `agui_parity.rs`; the project manifest `acceptance/programme/S10.toml` carries the seventeen record checks. The content is accepted when the pack is consistent at the pinned snapshot and the suite assertions stand; the factory's manifest re-run is the close gate.

## Capabilities

A scoped tool surface, a durable conversation, a proposal and approval gate, exactly-once execution, fail-closed model access, and a coverage gate that fails by name. Each is delivered by a named module in the Phase C catalog and proven by a named suite; the proposal path additionally seals a secret-bearing input and records the target the invocation boundary will compare.

## Plan

The plan is `docs/plans/slices/S10-copilot-ag-ui.md`. Its build order is complete in the tree, with the migration renumbered to `0018_copilot.sql` and the extra suites added after the plan. This brief is the retrospective reading of it; the chat UI, the deployed copilot run and the live AG-UI consumer question stay S12 and S14 work, and the tranche-6 review is the project's closure forum.

# Evidence — S10 Copilot / AG-UI (retrospective, 2026-11-27)

## Claim

S10 delivers the copilot's one action surface. A scripted session opens a conversation and runs a read tool; a must-decide tool call becomes one pending `approval(kind='copilot.action')` with zero invocations; an authorised decision executes the action once and the second decision changes nothing; a reconnect replays the turn once; a low-scope principal sees the same omitted tools on `/api/copilot/actions` and `/mcp`; an unavailable router fails the turn with zero tool invocations; and every mutating operation resolves to an action or the declared `copilot.chat` exemption.

## Evidence

`crates/api/tests/copilot_session.rs` runs the read-tool session. `copilot_surface.rs` asserts the two surfaces are the same set, that a low-scope principal omits the tool, and that the known omitted name is `403 action-forbidden` on HTTP and an `isError` tool result on `/mcp`. `copilot_proposal.rs` asserts one pending approval with no invocation and the per-turn unique index. `copilot_approve.rs` asserts one invocation after approval and no second effect. `copilot_destructive.rs` asserts the recorded target, the rejected proposal and the foreign-approval refusal. `copilot_crash_replay.rs`, `copilot_replay.rs` and `copilot_reap.rs` cover replay and interruption. `copilot_turn.rs`, `copilot_retry.rs`, `copilot_rounds.rs`, `copilot_truncated.rs` and `copilot_bad_args.rs` cover the fail-closed model boundary. `copilot_identity.rs` is the S16 W7 recipe identity and ledger proof. `agui_parity.rs` pins the eight golden frames. `crates/actions/tests/copilot_coverage.rs` is the coverage gate, including the secret-redaction projection test.

## Verification

The plan's gate commands are `cargo test -p conveyor-api --test copilot_session --test copilot_surface --test copilot_replay --test copilot_turn`, `cargo test -p conveyor-api --test copilot_proposal --test copilot_approve --test copilot_reap --test agui_parity`, and `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test copilot_coverage`, followed by clippy on the workspace. This retrospective pack does not claim a fresh local compile or test run; the repository's preflight and the PR's CI are the compile-and-run gate, and the content checker verifies the pack against the pinned snapshot. The pre-pack receipt is `docs/evidence/rework/S10.json` and is red on lifecycle checks; the pack supplies the missing set.

## Links

The plan is `docs/plans/slices/S10-copilot-ag-ui.md`; the migration is `migrations/0018_copilot.sql`; the modules are `crates/actions/src/agent_surface.rs`, `crates/api/src/copilot/turns.rs`, `crates/api/src/copilot/proposal.rs`, `crates/api/src/copilot/agui.rs`, `crates/store/src/copilot.rs` and `crates/actions/src/integrations/inference.rs`. The record's manifest is `acceptance/programme/S10.toml`; its PI cadence, PI plan and PI objectives checks are the programme-level records it reads, and the tranche-6 review is the closure forum.

## Gap

No deployed copilot, chat UI or production router run is claimed; those are S12 and S14 work. The AG-UI adapter's live consumer is not proven by the golden-frame suite and stays an open risk. The plan's `0011_copilot.sql` and `crates/store/src/jobs/kind/copilot.rs` paths do not exist in the tree; the built migration is 0018 and the sweeps live in `crates/store/src/schedule.rs`. The identity suites are S16 W7 work carried under the copilot prefix and are not re-scoped to S10. No other gap is claimed closed.
